LSTM networks are a specialized form of RNN designed to overcome the vanishing gradient problem (Hochreiter 1998). They incorporate memory cells and gating mechanisms (input, output, and forget gates) to regulate the flow of information, allowing the capture of long-term dependencies in sequential data (Trinh et al. 2018), making them particularly suitable for predicting inverter performance where past operational dynamics influence future behavior. The flexibility of LSTMs in handling variable-length sequences and learning complex temporal patterns has made them a standard benchmark in time-series prediction tasks (Siami-Namini, Tavakoli, and Namin 2018). The LSTM architecture implemented in this study consists of an input layer that processes five features, one single layer con- taining 50 hidden units, and it was trained over 200 epochs with a dynamic learning rate from 0.01 to 0.0005. The training process required 196 seconds, resulting in a training L2 loss of 3.6e-5, and a test L2 loss of 2.6e-4. GRUs are a streamlined variant of the LSTM architecture (Chung et al. 2014). They combine the input and forget gates into a single update gate, resulting in fewer parameters while still maintaining the capacity to capture long-term dependencies. Due to their simpler structure, GRUs often exhibit faster training times and require fewer computa- tional resources (Yang, Yu, and Zhou 2020). The GRU architecture implemented in this study, like the LSTM one, consists of an input layer that processes five features, one single layer containing 50 hidden units, and it was trained over 200 epochs with a dynamic learning rate from 0.01 to 0.0005. The training process required 167 seconds, result- ing in a training L2 loss of 3.5e-5, and a test L2 loss of 2.6e-4. For simplicity, we only show here the qualitative results for the GRU model, but similar performances are obtained with all the ML models. Transformers rely on self-attention mechanisms rather than recurrence to encode sequential information (Vaswani et al. 2017). This design allows the model to process all inputs simultaneously, providing significant speed advantages through parallelization and effectively capturing long-range dependencies, with remarkable results in various time- series forecasting applications (Wen et al. 2022). The Transformers architecture was implemented with one layer containing eight attention heads, trained for 200 epochs with a dynamic learning rate from 0.01 to 0.0005. The training process required 220 seconds, leading to a training L2 loss of 1.1e-4 and a test L2 loss of 3.2e-4.
